subject.title: Fallback turns can re-execute work already reported as completed (semantic recursive task execution)

question: Should #92011 land as a scoped embedded sessions_spawn mitigation while #92271 stays open for gateway, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native follow-up, or should maintainers require one shared work-spawning policy before any merge?
rationale: The remaining scope crosses OpenClaw embedded/gateway delegation paths and Codex-owned native spawn_agent behavior, so automation cannot choose the product boundary or release sequencing safely.

options.title: Accept scoped mitigation
options.body: Merge or finish #92011 for the embedded sessions_spawn guard, require explicit follow-up ownership for the remaining surfaces, and keep this issue open until that scope is closed.

options.title: Require shared policy first
options.body: Hold #92011 until fallback+completion turn context gates every OpenClaw work-delegating surface in one coherent implementation.

options.title: Split Codex upstream
options.body: Define OpenClaw-owned surfaces here and open or track a separate upstream Codex-native spawn_agent item before deciding this issue can close.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped mitigation
recommendation.body: Merge or finish #92011 for the embedded sessions_spawn guard, require explicit follow-up ownership for the remaining surfaces, and keep this issue open until that scope is closed.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned to #92011 and has recent fallback-path history, making him the best available owner for the scope decision.
